candidates.attacker_control: Indirect: the browser controls the value only when the application wires request-derived data into the tag, e.g. <s:i18n name="%{#parameters.bundle}"> or a request-bound bean property. I18n.setName stores the raw attribute (lines 153-156); I18n.start() resolves it with findString() (including %{...} altSyntax evaluation) and reuses the resolved string unescaped inside the OGNL expression at line 113. Request-driven tag attributes are a documented Struts usage pattern and the premise of this vulnerability class.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: No quote escaping and no bundle-name validation exists in I18n; Component.findValue only strips %{...}/${...} altSyntax wrappers and then evaluates. SecurityMemberAccess blocks static access by default and excludes java.lang.*/ognl.* packages, and DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker excludes #context/#_memberAccess, raising the exploit bar; however those exclusions are not applied as validation of this internally built expression, so injection remains (property traversal and non-excluded class/method access). Repository demo apps use literal bundle names, so exploitation requires the documented request-driven usage rather than default demo configuration, which is why confidence is medium.
candidates.impact: Expression-language injection in the framework rendering path: arbitrary OGNL evaluation against the action ValueStack. Depending on sandbox state this enables disclosure of application/session data, property/method invocation on reachable objects, and potentially remote code execution (the classic Struts tag-expression RCE pattern); at minimum a serious injection primitive chainable with the OGNL sandbox weaknesses present in this version.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Application passes request-influenced data into <s:i18n name>. 2) The i18n tag is rendered so I18n.start() executes. 3) OGNL sandbox restrictions (struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false, SecurityMemberAccess excludedClasses/excludedPackageNamePatterns, DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker) constrain but do not eliminate the injection; method calls on non-excluded classes and property traversal remain evaluable, and sandbox bypasses have historically been possible in this version line.
candidates.root_cause: I18n.java builds an OGNL expression by string concatenation: line 112 resolves the tag's name attribute via findString(), and line 113 does ResourceBundle bundle = (ResourceBundle) findValue("getTexts('" + name + "')");. The resolved bundle name is inserted unescaped and unvalidated into a single-quoted OGNL string literal, so a name containing a single quote (e.g. x')...(ognl)...(' ) terminates the literal and appends attacker-controlled OGNL that Component.findValue() evaluates via ValueStack.findValue().
candidates.title: OGNL expression injection via the <s:i18n> tag's name attribute (I18n component)
candidates.trace: Tag attribute -> I18n.setName -> I18n.start(): String name = this.findString(this.name, "name", ...) (I18n.java:112) -> ResourceBundle bundle = (ResourceBundle) findValue("getTexts('" + name + "')") (I18n.java:113) -> Component.findValue(String) (Component.java:268) -> getStack().findValue(expr, throwExceptionOnELFailure) (Component.java:275) -> OGNL parses and evaluates the composed expression against the action ValueStack. A quote in name escapes the string literal and the remainder is interpreted as OGNL.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Exact CVE/S2 bulletin attribution (i18n-tag OGNL injection fixed in the 2.3.20.x cycle) could not be verified offline; the dataset target could instead be a 2014 tag-XSS advisory whose fix is in an excluded file type. Whether real applications feed request data into <s:i18n name> is application-dependent, and a full RCE chain against this version's OGNL sandbox was not demonstrated.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-917 Expression Language Injection / CWE-94 Code Injection (OGNL)

coverage_summary: Covered the 2,866 model-visible files with targeted reading of action mapping/invocation (DefaultActionMapper, DefaultActionProxy, DefaultActionInvocation, ActionConfig, XmlConfigurationProvider), OGNL security (OgnlUtil, OgnlValueStack, SecurityMemberAccess, pattern checkers), interceptors (Parameters, Cookie, StaticParameters, FileUpload, Debugging), multipart handling (JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper, Dispatcher.wrapRequest), URL/rendering components (Component, I18n, URL, Anchor, Text, DefaultUrlHelper, ServletUrlRenderer, UIBean) and several plugins (rest, json, javatemplates). Not exhaustive across every plugin/app module or every interceptor/result.
limitations: No test sources, Freemarker (.ftl), JSP (.jsp), Velocity (.vm) or DTD files are present in the visible snapshot, so template-level XSS/expression issues and defaults documented only in struts-2.3.dtd could not be inspected; a template-based fix would be invisible here.
Exact commit/version provenance cannot be confirmed; pom version 2.3.20-SNAPSHOT plus 2014-era dependencies suggests a pre-2.3.20 tree, but the case's assigned CVE was not verifiable offline.
No execution, build, dependency-resolution or scanner results; findings are source-level only and not runtime-confirmed.
OGNL sandbox exploitability (static-method bypass chains) was reasoned about from source, not demonstrated; the i18n candidate requires an application that passes request data into the tag name.

rejected_leads.lead: DMI method-name OGNL evaluation: DefaultActionInvocation.invokeAction() (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/DefaultActionInvocation.java:423) evaluates ognlUtil.getValue(methodName + "()", ...), and DefaultActionMapper (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/DefaultActionMapper.java:136-141, 269-284) accepts arbitrary method names via method: / name!method when struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation=true; ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod() only rejects when a package is strict and struts-default.xml does not enable strict method invocation.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires non-default DMI enablement; public S2-032 fix cycle (2.3.29/2.5.2, 2016) postdates this 2.3.20-SNAPSHOT tree, so unlikely to be this case's regression. Recorded as a lead, not the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Content-Type OGNL evaluation: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/multipart/JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:118-124) passes e.getMessage() (containing the raw attacker-controlled Content-Type for InvalidContentTypeException) as the default message to LocalizedTextUtil.findText(), and LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/util/LocalizedTextUtil.java:660-683) OGNL-evaluates it via TextParseUtil.translateVariables; reachable by default because Dispatcher.wrapRequest() (Dispatcher.java:828-844) parses any Content-Type containing multipart/form-data and StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter (lines 89-91) creates the ValueStack before wrapping. This is the S2-045/CVE-2017-5638 root cause (unauthenticated RCE).
rejected_leads.reason: Root cause predates this snapshot and the public CVE/fix belong to the 2017 cycle (2.3.32/2.5.10.2), inconsistent with a 2.3.20-SNAPSHOT vulnerable commit; kept as a rejected lead but a severe hardening issue.

rejected_leads.lead: REST plugin XStream deserialization: plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java uses a default XStream instance without type restrictions (S2-052-style RCE via crafted XML).
rejected_leads.reason: Plugin-scoped and tied to a much later fix cycle (2.5.13/2.3.34); not the strongest era-consistent candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Inconsistent output-escaping heuristics: DefaultUrlHelper.buildUrl()'s <script check (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/views/util/DefaultUrlHelper.java:182-186), UIBean.ensureAttributeSafelyNotEscaped() (UIBean.java:905-917) and javatemplates handlers (SubmitHandler.java:85, AbstractMessageListHandler.java:43-56).
rejected_leads.reason: Real exploitability depends on Freemarker/JSP templates excluded from this snapshot; no concrete request-to-sink path could be established in visible code.

summary: Reviewed the assigned Struts 2.3.20-SNAPSHOT source tree (xwork-core + core + plugins; 2,866 model-visible files). Strongest era-consistent issue: an OGNL expression-injection sink in the <s:i18n> component, where the tag's bundle name is concatenated unescaped into an OGNL expression that is evaluated on the ValueStack. This matches the tag-level OGNL injection class (S2-027 / CVE-2014-7809 family; exact CVE not verifiable offline). Other present issues (DMI method-name OGNL evaluation, Content-Type default-message OGNL evaluation, REST XStream deserialization) are listed as rejected leads because they are config-dependent or belong to later fix cycles than this snapshot.
